section: Administrative changes - civil services, army reorganisation, police, judiciary, local self-government (Ripon)
subsections: Local self-government - first corporation, Cantonments Act, Mayo, Ripon

accepted.s: The first municipal corporation in India was established at which place in 1688?
accepted.x: The first municipal corporation in India was established at Madras in 1688.
accepted.tq: Use the place-year association to distinguish the first corporation from the later corporations at Bombay and Calcutta.
accepted.sec: Local self-government - first corporation, Cantonments Act, Mayo, Ripon  [APPSC]

accepted.s: In which year were municipal corporations established at Bombay and Calcutta?
accepted.x: Municipal corporations were established at Bombay and Calcutta in 1726, after the first corporation at Madras in 1688.
accepted.tq: Separate the close chronological milestones by matching the year with the two later-established corporations.
accepted.sec: Local self-government - first corporation, Cantonments Act, Mayo, Ripon  [APPSC]

accepted.s:
Consider the following statements regarding Lord Mayo's Resolution of 1870:
1. It marked the first step towards financial decentralisation.
2. It bifurcated central and provincial finances.
3. It gave provinces certain services to administer.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: All three statements are correct. Mayo's Resolution of 1870 began financial decentralisation, divided central and provincial finances, and assigned certain services to the provinces.
accepted.tq: Test the cluster of connected features rather than relying on the year alone.
accepted.sec: Local self-government - first corporation, Cantonments Act, Mayo, Ripon  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Which one of the following was NOT one of the services specifically associated with the provincial responsibility under Lord Mayo's financial decentralisation scheme?
accepted.x: Police, jails and education were among the services assigned to the provinces. Foreign affairs was not one of the locally administered services listed under the scheme.
accepted.tq: Find the item outside the closely related group of provincial administrative services.
accepted.sec: Local self-government - first corporation, Cantonments Act, Mayo, Ripon  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Under Lord Mayo's financial decentralisation scheme, the provinces were expected to meet their responsibilities primarily by
o: transferring their services to district courts
receiving fixed grants and raising local taxes
accepted.x: The provinces received fixed grants for administering certain services and were also instructed to raise local taxes.
accepted.tq: Apply the financial arrangement to identify the combination of grants and local taxation.
accepted.sec: Local self-government - first corporation, Cantonments Act, Mayo, Ripon  [APPSC]

accepted.s:
With reference to Lord Ripon's Resolution of 1882, consider the following statements:
1. It provided for an elected non-official majority in local bodies.
2. It emphasised local autonomy.
3. It envisaged the participation of non-official members in local boards, district boards, municipal councils and village panchayats.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: Ripon's Resolution included an elected non-official majority, local autonomy and wider participation of non-official members in the principal local institutions.
accepted.tq: Check whether each statement captures a separate institutional feature of the 1882 Resolution.
accepted.sec: Local self-government - first corporation, Cantonments Act, Mayo, Ripon  [APPSC]

accepted.s:
Arrange the following developments in chronological order:
A. Government of India Act, 1935 made local self-government a provincial subject
B. Lord Ripon's Resolution on local self-government
C. Government of India Act, 1919 treated local self-government as a transferred subject
D. Lord Mayo's Resolution on financial decentralisation
accepted.x: The correct sequence is Mayo's Resolution of 1870, Ripon's Resolution of 1882, the Government of India Act of 1919, and the Government of India Act of 1935.
accepted.tq: Fix the sequence by first placing the dated Mayo and Ripon resolutions, then the two constitutional Acts.
accepted.sec: Local self-government - first corporation, Cantonments Act, Mayo, Ripon  [APPSC]

accepted.s: The Royal Commission on Decentralisation, constituted during 1907–09, was chaired by
accepted.x: C.E.H. Hobhouse chaired the Royal Commission on Decentralisation of 1907–09.
accepted.tq: Discriminate between the reforming Viceroys and the chairman of the later commission.
accepted.sec: Local self-government - first corporation, Cantonments Act, Mayo, Ripon  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Which of the following recommendations was associated with the Royal Commission on Decentralisation of 1907–09?
o: Making local self-government an exclusively central subject
Strengthening local institutions and village panchayats
Replacing municipal councils with military boards
accepted.x: The Commission recommended strengthening local institutions, including village panchayats.
accepted.tq: Identify the recommendation that directly advances decentralisation instead of reversing it.
accepted.sec: Local self-government - first corporation, Cantonments Act, Mayo, Ripon  [APPSC]

accepted.s: What significant change concerning local self-government was introduced by the Government of India Act, 1935?
o: It made local self-government a provincial subject.
It placed local self-government under the exclusive control of the Governor-General.
It transferred local self-government to the Central Legislature.
It abolished village panchayats in the provinces.
accepted.x: The Government of India Act, 1935 made local self-government a provincial subject.
accepted.tq: Match the constitutional Act with the level of government to which the subject was assigned.
accepted.sec: Local self-government - first corporation, Cantonments Act, Mayo, Ripon  [APPSC]

accepted.s:
Consider the following statements about the development of local self-government:
1. Village panchayats were set up in several provinces after the Government of India Act, 1919.
2. Local bodies after Ripon's Resolution were entirely free from colonial official control.
3. Local bodies were often starved of funds.
4. Non-official members entered village panchayats, municipal councils and district boards after 1882.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: Statements 1, 3 and 4 are correct. Statement 2 is false because local bodies continued to be controlled by colonial officials and were also constrained by inadequate funds.
accepted.tq: Reject the absolute claim of complete freedom while retaining the institutional changes and criticism.
accepted.sec: Local self-government - first corporation, Cantonments Act, Mayo, Ripon  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Lord Mayo's tenure, during which he introduced financial decentralisation and conducted the first census of India, was
accepted.x: Lord Mayo served from 1869 to 1872. During this period, the financial decentralisation Resolution of 1870 was introduced and the first census was conducted in 1871.
accepted.tq: Link the tenure with the two dated developments to avoid confusing adjacent three-year ranges.
accepted.sec: Local self-government - first corporation, Cantonments Act, Mayo, Ripon  [APPSC]

accepted.s: In addition to financial decentralisation, Lord Mayo's administration is associated with
o: the transfer of local self-government to the provinces in 1935
the Royal Commission on Decentralisation of 1907–09
the first municipal corporation at Madras in 1688
a statistical survey of India and the first census in 1871
accepted.x: Lord Mayo also undertook a statistical survey of India and conducted the first census in 1871.
accepted.tq: Separate Mayo's statistical and census initiatives from reforms belonging to other years and administrators.
accepted.sec: Local self-government - first corporation, Cantonments Act, Mayo, Ripon  [APPSC]

accepted.s:
Assertion (A): The local self-government institutions introduced during the colonial period did not enjoy complete autonomy.
Reason (R): They were often starved of funds and remained subject to the control of colonial officials.

Choose the correct answer using the code given below.
o: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
accepted.x: Both statements are true, and inadequate finances together with continued official control explains why the local bodies did not possess complete autonomy.
accepted.tq: Test whether the stated institutional limitation is directly explained by the administrative and financial constraints.
accepted.sec: Local self-government - first corporation, Cantonments Act, Mayo, Ripon  [APPSC]
